definitions.gloss: the first train of the day
definitions.explanation: the earliest train service on a particular route or line

examples.japanese: {始発電車|しはつでんしゃ}に{乗|の}って{空港|くうこう}に{向|む}かった。
examples.english: I took the first train to head to the airport.

examples.japanese: {始発電車|しはつでんしゃ}は5{時|じ}に{出|で}る。
examples.english: The first train leaves at 5 o'clock.

examples.japanese: {終電|しゅうでん}を{逃|のが}して{始発電車|しはつでんしゃ}を{待|ま}った。
examples.english: I missed the last train and waited for the first train.

notes:
TRANSPORTATION VOCABULARY:
{始発電車|しはつでんしゃ} refers to the first train of the day on a particular line or route.

SHORT FORM:
Often shortened to {始発|しはつ}.

TYPICAL TIMES:
{始発電車|しはつでんしゃ} usually runs between 4:30-5:30 AM depending on the line.

WHO USES IT:
- Early morning workers
- Travelers heading to airports
- People who missed the last train and waited overnight
- Early risers wanting to avoid crowds

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {始発電車|しはつでんしゃ}に{乗|の}る - to catch the first train
- {始発電車|しはつでんしゃ}を{待|ま}つ - to wait for the first train
- {始発|しはつ}で{帰|かえ}る - to go home on the first train (after staying out all night)

RELATED:
- {終電|しゅうでん} - last train
- {始発|しはつ} - first train (short form); first departure
- {通勤電車|つうきんでんしゃ} - commuter train
- {早朝|そうちょう} - early morning
